text: Hello everyone, welcome to my class.Is everything ready?Have you got your student's notebook and worksheet ready?请准备好你的课本、笔记本以及这一课时的worksheet.Let's get started.Last period, we talked about what we know about newspapers and what we want to know about them.Some of you might be wondering what a school newspaper should be like and what it should include.Before our further discussion, I'd like you to think about this question.What would you like to read in a school newspaper?Take a few seconds and write down your ideas.Kevin, what would you like to read?I prefer to read interviews with popular teachers and star students, and I won't miss any school advice in the newspaper.For example, study tips before exams are always helpful.Good point.You like to read interviews and school advice.What about you, Benson?I like to read heated debates in the school newspaper.We students voice our opinions on topics we care about.What else do you like to read?I also like to read reviews of books, music or movies that appeal to us teenagers.For example, the latest releases of cartoon films or popular novels.It is interesting to know what other students think of the same book or movie.Well, you know the word review.We write reviews to give opinions about a new book, film or music.Nathan, do you have anything to share with us?I like to read articles on the same topic, but written by different authors.These articles are put in one section to provide detailed information on one topic.Oh, these articles are called features or feature articles.Reading features enables us to know about a topic from different perspectives.We may know people's different opinions on the same topic.Anything else?I also like to read news reports in the school newspaper.News reports update me on what is happening on campus and outside school.Right.News reports in a school newspaper focus on school events and other issues students care about.What school events do you think school newspapers should report on?Benson, what do you come up with?School newspapers report on school outings and field trips.For example, the visit to the water treatment works.Great.Lucy, any other school events can you think of?We have competitions of all kinds, such as the speech contest and the singing contest.Competitions?Good.What else?Besides, the sports meeting and the art festival are two big school events.How often do the sports meeting and the school art festival take place?Once a year, right?So they are annual events.They take place once a year.Say after me.Annual Usually, the school art festivals end with a big show.Students and teachers sing, dance, play musical instruments and so on to show various talents.This performance is called talent show.Any other annual school events?Mason?Some ceremonies like the graduation ceremony and our 14th birthday celebration.Another big event is the Youth League party at which you join the Youth League.To be a Youth League member is something you are proud of.These are what school newspapers are most likely to report on.Think about another two questions.Who write articles for school newspapers and what do they write?Do you have any ideas, Kevin?I think student journalists write news reports for school newspapers.Journalists, we also say reporters, and editors sometimes write articles as well.Both reporters and editors write news reports, interviews, features and so on.Nathan, what do you say?We students, I mean students who are not working for the school newspaper write for school newspapers too.We write reviews and some interesting stories.Non-journalist students write about their personal experiences to share with other students.And as Nathan said, you also write other things like reviews.We also have articles written by teachers or even the headmaster.They write letters to students, appeals, comments and so on.School newspapers include various kinds of articles to attract different readers.Today, we'll listen to an article in a school newspaper.Let's look at the title.My most exciting day.Who wrote the article?Robert.Who is Robert?A student journalist or a non-journalist student?No idea?You can make a guess.We will go back to this question later.Then think about these two questions.The first question, what does Robert probably write about his most exciting day?Benson?Probably he writes about what he did on his most exciting day.Perhaps he did something exciting.Maybe he writes something about his field trip to a publishing house.Very likely.By the way, what makes your school day exciting, Benson?A lot of things make my school day exciting.For example, winning a competition, delivering a speech successfully, putting on a performance and so on.All of these things are quite meaningful and they make your school days colorful.Maybe they make Robert's school day exciting too.Let's move on.What do you want to know about Robert's most exciting day?Lucy?I want to know when his most exciting day was, where he spent that day, who he spent the day with and what he did.Excellent.I also want to know why it was his most exciting day.These are all key elements of an event.Let's listen to Robert's article and find answers to these questions.While you're listening, don't forget to write down the answers on your worksheet, task one.Are you ready?My most exciting day was in November last year at the annual youth league party in the park.The chief secretary started the party at 11 a.There were many league members from all over the city, about 20,000 in all.It was very exciting.First, we all said our league promise.Then we marched around the park.After that, we all formed into big circles and danced.A helicopter flew over us and took a photograph from the air.I have a copy of that photograph in my bedroom now.After that, we had some activities.There were 90 game stalls altogether.I helped at a game.In the game, people tried to throw table tennis balls into glass jars.It was good fun.I also had time to walk around and look at the other games.There were some good shows too.There was a talent show and a competition for people wearing the national costumes of different countries.At the end, we gathered in groups and sang some songs.It was wonderful to see so many friends together and I really enjoyed that day.Shall we check the answers?The first one.When was Robert's most exciting day?It was in November last year.The article doesn't mention the exact date.Number two.Where did Robert spend the day?He spent the day in the park.Number three.Who did Robert spend the day with?Number four.Why was that day so special to Robert?He took part in many different activities that day.But most importantly, he joined the Youth League.He is a Youth League member now.One more question to answer.What did Robert do on his most exciting day?The first question.You will find out soon.I'd like to show you some pictures first.What are the students doing in this picture?The students are dancing in circles.What do you see in picture B?We can see different kinds of games.Actually, they are game stores at a school fair.We also have food stores.These stores are always set up by school clubs or different classes for children to have fun or sometimes for fundraising.Look at picture C.The students are walking in line.We can say they are marching.Here, march is a verb.It means to walk with regular steps as a group, like soldiers.Picture D.It is what we have discussed.What are the students doing in picture E?They are singing together, probably in a choir.Look at picture F.What is the boy doing?Why is he raising his arm?Look at the flag.Right, he is probably raising his arm.Let's move on to picture G.Are the students wearing everyday clothes?No, they are wearing national costumes, clothes of different countries.CostumeCostumeCostumeCostumeCostumeCostumeCostumeCostumeCostumeCostumeCostumeCostumeThe Chief Secretary started the party at 11am.There were many League members from all over the city.About 20,000 in why.Benson, would you like to have a try?Robert's most exciting day was in November last year.He spent the day with other 20,000 league membersat the annual Youth League of China.He spent the day with other 20,000 league membersat the annual Youth League party in the park.First, they set their league promise.Then, they marched around the park.After that, they danced in big circles.When they were dancing, a helicopter took a picture from the air.After that, they had some activities.There were 90 game stores in all.Robert helped at a game store.He threw table tennis balls into glass jars.Then, to be with so many friends on such an exciting day.Good job!You included all the important information.Now, let's go back to the question I asked at the beginning of the class.Is Robert a student journalist or a non-journalist student?I think he is a non-journalist student,because a journalist usually writes articles in the third person.Another question for you to think about.Will Robert's article go to the front page or news section?Why or why not?Kevin, what's your opinion on this?I don't think the article will go to the front page or news section,because what he wrote is his personal experience,and the article doesn't look like a news report at all.Here comes the question.What should a news report be like?Let's take this news report as an example.A news report usually includes a headline,which is the title printed in large letters,and a byline, which tells us about the author.The first paragraph is called lead,the middle part is called body,and the finishing part is a tail.Let's take a close look at these parts.A good headline should catch the reader's attentionin interesting and powerful language,and sum up the story in a few words.That means the readers can know what the news report is aboutjust at one glance.The byline includes the writer's name and specialty,for example, sports reporter.A good lead should include important informationthat explains what has happened,and answer as many of these six questions as possible.Who, what, where, why, when, and how.Even if the readers stop reading at this point,they still know roughly what happened in the story.The next part is the body.It adds more details and background information to the lead.And it usually includes quotes from people involved in the story.Quotes are what people say in direct speech.Details and quotes make the report interesting to read.The last part is called tail.The least important information is added here,and it sums up the story or hints at what might happen
